ISTRESS-STALE-APPROVAL-006-CURRENT-GAP and ISTRESS-STALE-APPROVAL-006-POLICY instead support a narrower certification position: certification is supportable only if the packet is treated as caveated and only if the current release documentation is required to state the clinical-trial intake weakness plainly for that named use case. 3. Monitoring also needs to stay in its lane. ISTRESS-STALE-APPROVAL-006-CONTEXT shows an informal monitoring concept exists, but I am not offering that as policy satisfaction for the pre-launch requirement. It is relevant only to post-launch risk handling and to why the remaining risk is governable after disclosure, not to prove the disclosure already exists. 4. The suspicious score appears to over-weight the absence of attached wording into a conclusion that certification itself is categorically unsupported. The admissible record does support current launch readiness at the aggregate level and no severity-one rehearsal incidents via ISTRESS-STALE-APPROVAL-006-AGGREGATE-PASS, while ISTRESS-STALE-APPROVAL-006-HF-CONTENT and ISTRESS-STALE-APPROVAL-006-NIST-MEASURE support a certification frame centered on current evaluation results, limitations, and monitored deployment. The open gap is the wording/attachment state, not whether the only permissible outcome is escalation. 5. So the clean position is not unconditional compliance. It is caveated compliance: certify_model with the audit packet explicitly bounded to current-release results, explicit subgroup disclosure, and no reliance on stale approval or informal monitoring as substitutes for those items.
